newsitem.title: USA: German banks seek better repo trade conditions.
newsitem.headline: German banks seek better repo trade conditions.

text.p: The German banking association said on Tuesday that the abolition of minimum reserves requirements on repo transactions would allow Germany to pull back some of this business from London.

Karl-Heinz Wessel, president of the association, told a news conference in Washington held on the sidelines of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank annual meeting, that necessary changes should be made as soon as possible.
"The framework for a competitive financial centre should be created today," he said, adding such changes should not be delayed until the start of European monetary union in 1999.
"One example would be the lifting of the minimum reserve requirement for repo business, which would not negatively affect the capability of the Bundesbank to conduct monetary policy," he said.
"That would be an important step towards regaining lost ground against London," he added.

The fact that repo transactions are subject to reserve requirements means hardly any mark repo dealing is conducted in Germany. The Bundesbank is known to have been examining the impact of the abolition of reserve levies on such business but no decisions have been made as yet.
